title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF TEACHERS’ DAY
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF TEACHERS’ DAY
sources.evidenceText:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu has greeted teachers across the country on the eve of Teachers’ Day.
In a message, the President has said, “On the occasion of Teachers’ Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all our teachers across the country. Teachers’ Day is observed to mark the birth anniversary of the former President of India, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan who was a great author and philosopher. He was also an extraordinary teacher. On this occasion, I pay my humble tributes to him.
Teachers, through their guidance and mentorship, play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character. It is their duty to guide students to become good human beings. A dedicated and caring teacher can recognise the unique potential of students, serve as a source of inspiration and encourage them to strive for excellence.
The teachers should continually update their knowledge, embrace technology and adopt innovative teaching methods. They should promote independent thinking and cultivate a spirit of enquiry among students.
I express my gratitude to all the dedicated teachers for their contribution. I wish that all teachers nurture enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights”.

title: NIFT joint convocation 2026 held in presence of Hon’ble President of India
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: NIFT joint convocation 2026 held in presence of Hon’ble President of India
sources.evidenceText:
Mumbai, 4 September 2026
A total of 315 graduating students from the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Mumbai participated in the NIFT Joint Convocation 2026 held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, on 31 August 2026. The Convocation brought together graduating students from 18 NIFT campuses across the country to celebrate their academic achievements and mark the beginning of their professional journeys.
The Convocation was graced by the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, as the Chief Guest. The Hon’ble Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh; Secretary (Textiles), Smt. Neelam Shami Rao; Director General, NIFT, Smt. Tanu Kashyap, IAS; members of the Board of Governors; Prof. Dr. Ajit Kumar Khare, Director, NIFT Mumbai; Directors of NIFT campuses and other distinguished dignitaries were also present.
Addressing the graduating students, the Hon’ble President encouraged them to remain globally competitive while staying connected with India’s cultural heritage and values. She appreciated NIFT’s Craft Cluster Initiative for supporting weavers and artisans through design and market linkages. She also stressed the importance of sustainability, use of local materials and recycling of textile waste. The President called upon the graduates to support traditional artisans and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 through innovation, social responsibility and inclusive growth.
The Hon’ble Union Minister of Textiles urged the graduates to dream big, work hard and contribute to the development of a Viksit Bharat. The Secretary (Textiles) congratulated the students and encouraged them to pursue continuous learning and skill development.
The ceremony also recognised the achievements of NIFT Mumbai students through 10 Gold Medals, 31 Graduation Show Awards and 16 Meritorious Awards for excellence, creativity, innovation and professional merit.
The Director General, NIFT, administered the pledge and symbolically conferred the degrees. Campus-wise degree distribution ceremonies were subsequently held. The Convocation concluded with the National Song and National Anthem.
* * *
PIB Mumbai | Robin Singh/ Darshana Rane

Vice-President of India and Ex-Officio Chancellor of Panjab University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated advanced scientific infrastructure facilities at Panjab University, Chandigarh, today.

title: Dr Jitendra Singh and French Minister Philippe Baptiste hold virtual meeting; discuss upcoming 'International Space Summit' and France’s participation in 'Bengaluru Space Expo'
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: Dr Jitendra Singh and French Minister Philippe Baptiste hold virtual meeting; discuss upcoming 'International Space Summit' and France’s participation in 'Bengaluru Space Expo'
sources.evidenceText:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, held a bilateral meeting virtually with France’s Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space, Prof Philippe Baptiste, with the two sides agreeing to further deepen India-France cooperation in space, including in human spaceflight, advanced space technologies and greater engagement between their space agencies and industries.
The discussions took place ahead of the International Space Summit, scheduled for September 9-10, 2026 in Paris, and the Bengaluru Space Expo, scheduled for September 7-9, 2026. Both sides discussed India’s participation in the Paris Summit and France’s participation in the Bengaluru Space Expo, along with the forthcoming visit of Prof. Baptiste to India later this month.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India looks forward to participating in the International Space Summit and to further strengthening its longstanding space partnership with France. He said the Summit’s focus on space science, technology and applications, space economy and secure space provide an important platform for international dialogue and cooperation on the future of the space sector.
India welcomed the proposed Summit deliverables on the sustainable use of outer space, accessibility, openness and integrity of space-based scientific data, and support for the International Telecommunication Union’s regulatory framework for frequency management. Dr. Jitendra Singh conveyed India’s readiness to exchange views with the French side during the finalisation of these initiatives.
A key focus of the discussions was India’s contribution to the Paris Summit. Chairman, ISRO/Secretary, Department of Space has been invited to deliver the opening keynote on India’s future human spaceflight in Low Earth Orbit. Dr. Jitendra Singh also conveyed that, if considered useful by the French side, members of the Indian delegation could make presentations on additional areas, including design and manufacturing technologies in space, connectivity from space and exploration beyond the International Space Station.
Prof. Philippe Baptiste expressed France’s desire to further strengthen and accelerate the existing India-France cooperation in space. He also thanked India for the proposed video message from Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the Summit and welcomed continued consultations with the Indian side on the declarations proposed for adoption at the event.
The two sides also discussed France’s participation in the Bengaluru Space Expo and the opportunities for enhanced interaction between the two countries’ space agencies, industries and emerging space ecosystems.
Prof Baptiste is scheduled to visit India from September 28-30, 2026 and has expressed interest in visiting ISRO facilities in Bengaluru and meeting Dr. Jitendra Singh. The two sides agreed that their respective teams would continue consultations on possible areas of cooperation and on the additional presentations proposed for the Paris Summit.
India and France have shared a close space partnership spanning nearly six decades. Cooperation between ISRO and France’s CNES has included the joint satellite missions Megha-Tropiques and SARAL, while the two sides are also pursuing further cooperation in Earth observation and climate-related applications.
The meeting concluded with both sides reaffirming their commitment to further deepen India-France cooperation in space through innovation, research, human spaceflight, technology development and growing participation of the private space sector.
*****

title: ECL Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Drive Cleanliness, Sustainability and Operational Efficiency.

sources.evidenceText:
Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) has launched Special Campaign 6.0 under ‘Waste to Wealth’ theme by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances and ‘eWaste Management’ theme by Ministry of Coal, GoI, reaffirming its commitment towards enhancing workplace cleanliness, promoting sustainability and strengthening operational efficiency across the organisation.

title: India–EU FTA Opens Huge Opportunities for Farmers, MSMEs, Innovators, Startups and Businesses in India and Europe: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: India–EU FTA Opens Huge Opportunities for Farmers, MSMEs, Innovators, Startups and Businesses in India and Europe: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
sources.evidenceText:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that the India–European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA) opens huge opportunities for farmers, fishermen, MSMEs, small industries, innovators, startups, women entrepreneurs, manufacturers and service providers in India and Europe. Addressing the India–Belgium High-Level Dialogue on the India–EU FTA in Mumbai, in the presence of Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Belgium Mr. Bart De Wever and Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Shri Goyal said the agreement had been deftly negotiated while protecting sensitive sectors on both sides.
Shri Goyal said the India–EU FTA, which was in the making for 25 years before negotiations were concluded under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, brings together 2 billion people, representing a quarter of global GDP, a third of world trade and a market of USD 24 trillion. He said all 27 EU countries were on board, supportive and desirous of concluding the formalities and bringing the agreement into force at the earliest. He noted that such unanimous support was, as he understood, rare in the European context. Similarly, every section in India had supported the India–EU FTA wholeheartedly.
Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Belgium Mr. Bart De Wever said the India–EU FTA would strengthen trade and open doors for companies, young talent and investment, while making the two economies more resilient against disruptions. Highlighting the Port of Antwerp-Bruges as an important logistical link between India and Europe, he said the FTA would create opportunities in areas including diamonds, food processing, pharmaceuticals, maritime services, green hydrogen and infrastructure, and noted that tariffs on more than 95 per cent of Indian and European goods exports would be scrapped or reduced.
The Union Minister said India and Belgium have a significant opportunity to deepen economic cooperation as their economies complement each other across five major areas. He said India and Belgium could explore co-creation and design in gems and jewellery, including lab-grown diamonds as a new area of cooperation. He called for greater cooperation in technology and certification for mutual recognition, anchored around the main diamond centres of Antwerp, Mumbai and Surat.
Shri Goyal said Belgium’s world-class micro-electronics research could be paired with India’s scale, skills and talent to create a design-to-fabrication ecosystem in semiconductors. He said India’s Green Hydrogen Mission could power Europe through Antwerp-Bruges’ bunkering and green shipping infrastructure and called for deeper collaboration in this area.
Referring to the exchange of Memoranda of Understanding with John Cockerill, Shri Goyal said there was significant potential for cooperation in defence and advanced manufacturing, including counter-drone systems, electronic warfare, precision munitions and Western export corridors for India-designed BrahMos and Pinaka missiles. He said industrial alignment between India and Belgium had never run deeper. He also noted that John Cockerill makes ammunition for India’s Bofors guns. Given increased spending in Europe under the new conditions and India’s own security environment, he said there was tremendous potential to work together.
Shri Goyal also highlighted opportunities in agriculture and food processing, ranging from potato processing and cold chains to other areas of food processing. He said technology and sustainable agri-value chains could serve the entire world through Belgium and India.
The Union Minister said Belgium stands at the gateway of the opportunity created by the India–EU FTA. He noted that the Port of Antwerp-Bruges is Europe’s second-largest seaport and described it as the doorway through which the FTA’s promise would physically arrive in Europe or be dispatched to India. He said that by seamlessly combining Antwerp’s world-class inland barge, rail and road networks with Bruges’ seabridges, deepwater, roll-on/roll-off and automotive strengths, the port offers Indian exporters an unmatched route into the industrial and consumer heartlands of Europe.
Shri Goyal said India’s trade with the EU had already doubled over the last decade to nearly USD 140 billion. He said India and Belgium had a choice in the face of protectionism, broken supply chains, problems in food and fuel delivery, two wars, volatility, uncertainty and major challenges, to either be swept by the prevailing chaos or build islands of trust and predictability.
Quoting Belgian Nobel laureate Ilya Prigogine, Shri Goyal referred to the idea of “order emerging out of chaos” and said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister of Belgium and the Prime Minister of India, “we choose to build, we choose to connect, we choose to work together.”
Shri Goyal highlighted India’s expanding economic and technological capabilities and said that the Indian story had just begun. He noted that India is a USD 4 trillion economy today on a purchasing power parity basis and is already the world’s third-largest economy with a USD 20 trillion GDP on a PPP basis. He said the stated goal and collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians was to take the USD 4 trillion economy to a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047, when India celebrates 100 years of independence.
He said the roadmap had been made and the collective effort underway in India covered social upliftment, infrastructure creation, manufacturing at scale and creating a destination for global companies to come and work in India, design, co-design, co-create and co-manufacture. He said India and its partners could collectively work not only for Europe and India, but for the world as their market.
Shri Goyal highlighted India’s massive programme to promote the semiconductor industry. He said the first edition of Semicon India had been fully subscribed, with investors from around the world, while the second edition, Semicon India 2.0, had recently been launched with an outlay of USD 14 billion. Collectively, he said, the mission would catalyse nearly USD 70 billion worth of investments in the semiconductor space in India.
He said India’s AI Mission was up and running and serving startups, while the country was also active in its Critical Minerals Mission. He said India’s nuclear energy programme, through the Shanti Act, was now open to the private sector after 60 years, with a plan to build 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity over the next 20 years as baseload capacity to replace fossil fuel.
Shri Goyal said India’s space technology sector, currently at USD 8.5 billion, was expected to grow to USD 44 billion over the next eight years, largely driven by new private initiatives, startups, innovators and designers developing unique solutions. He said India had become only the third country in the world where a private company had launched a rocket into space and the first country where a private initiative had been successful on its very first attempt.
He also highlighted India’s recently launched USD 12 billion research and development fund for innovation. He said that, while USD 12 billion might appear modest from the European context, India’s purchasing power parity strength meant that the government’s contribution, coupled with private-sector investment and the capabilities of India’s academia, could collectively deliver the equivalent of USD 150 billion of innovation compared to what could be achieved in Europe, at a fraction of the cost and comparable to the best in the world.
Shri Goyal invited Belgium and the European Union to partner with India, saying that Belgium’s technology, innovation and capital could find a nest in India with its scale, talent, youthful energy, young population and decisive leadership.
The Union Minister said Maharashtra offered a very inviting place for business, describing it as India’s financial and commercial capital, its industrial capital and the fastest-growing economy in the country.
Shri Goyal invited Prime Minister De Wever and Belgian companies to engage with India with an open mind and open heart, supported by all the facilities required by modern industry. He said that underpinning all these opportunities were people, including the Indian community, students and researchers.
The Union Minister called for strengthening workforce mobility, mutual recognition of qualifications, joint skills development and dual-degree education programmes, particularly in sectors where Belgium faces a shortage of talent and youth.
Shri Goyal said India and Belgium share a very warm and enduring relationship dating back to 1947, when India gained independence. He noted that Belgium was one of the first European countries to establish diplomatic relations with independent India and said India would always be grateful to the Belgian people for the gesture.
The Union Minister thanked Prime Minister De Wever for his leadership, support and relentless pursuit of strengthening Belgium–India and EU–India relations, which had helped culminate a journey of 25 years.
Shri Goyal said that during his recent visit to Belgium, referred to during the programme, the real energy he felt was in Belgian enterprises. He said Belgium and India, together, could create an “absolutely unbeatable competition” by combining Belgian technology, innovation and capital with India’s scale, talent, youthful energy, young population and decisive leadership.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal drew an analogy with the formation of a diamond. He said a diamond is formed under tremendous pressure, deep under the ground, while lab-grown diamonds are formed through relentless processes involving carbon deposits. He said that in a world under pressure and turmoil, India and Belgium could form something equally enduring, beautiful and precious as a diamond.
“Let India and Belgium form something just as enduring, just as beautiful and precious as a diamond. A diamond not only for Belgium and India, a diamond not only for Europe, a diamond for the world,” Shri Goyal said.

title: First Batch of Corporate Mitra Course Commences with 2879 Learners registered
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: First Batch of Corporate Mitra Course Commences with 2879 Learners registered
sources.evidenceText:
The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) and the Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICoAI), under the guidance of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), has commenced the Corporate Mitra Course, with 2879 Learners registered in the first batch. The launch of the Corporate Mitra Learning Management System (LMS) marks the beginning of the structured learning and capability-development phase of the programme.
The Corporate Mitra initiative was announced by the Government of India in the Union Budget 2026-27 with the objective of creating a pool of trained and certified paraprofessionals who can support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in managing business and regulatory compliances. The programme brings together the professional expertise of ICAI, ICSI and ICoAI with the technology and academic support from IIT Madras, IIT Madras Pravartak and SWAYAM Plus.
The course was officially launched at an event organised at the ICAI Head Office in New Delhi, in the presence of Smt. Anita Shah Akella, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs; Shri Mahendra Kumar, Director-PI, Ministry of Corporate Affairs; and the leadership of ICAI, including Hon’ble President, ICAI, CA. Prasanna Kumar D; Hon’ble Vice-President, ICAI, CA. Mangesh P. Kinare and Hon’ble Secretary, ICAI, CA. (Dr.) Jai Kumar Batra.
The event was also attended by Hon’ble President, Institute of Cost Accountants of India, CMA Chittaranjan Chattopadhyay; Hon’ble Vice-President, Institute of Cost Accountants of India, CMA Manoj Kumar Anand; and other senior officials and representatives of all three Professional Institutes.
The Corporate Mitra Course aims to create a skilled cadre of certified para-professionals to provide affordable professional support to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), thereby promoting ease of doing business, employment generation and inclusive economic growth.
On this occasion, Smt. Anita Shah Akela, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs , said that “Corporate Mitra seeks to make compliance less intimidating and knowledge more accessible for entrepreneurs. She emphasised that the initiative is aimed at transforming compliance from a burden into an enabler of trust, transparency, accountability and orderly growth.”
The Corporate Mitra Course has a total duration of 12 months, divided into two stages. The first six months comprise approximately 150 hours of structured academic learning, delivered through recorded video lectures. This is followed by six months of on-the-job training in professional firms of members of ICAI, ICSI and ICoAI, providing learners with hands-on workplace experience.
The academic component has been designed to provide learners with a 360-degree understanding of MSME operations and support requirements. The digital learning ecosystem will provide learners with expert-led recorded lectures, reference material, assessments, announcements, FAQs and discussion forums.
The commencement of the Corporate Mitra Course marks an important step towards developing a skilled pool of paraprofessionals who can contribute to the growth and formalisation of India's MSME ecosystem.

title: CAQM conducts Special Industrial Inspection Drive in Nuh, Haryana; 17 out of 35 units found non-compliant
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: CAQM conducts Special Industrial Inspection Drive in Nuh, Haryana; 17 out of 35 units found non-compliant
sources.evidenceText:
As part of its continuing efforts to abate air pollution from industrial activities in the National Capital Region (NCR), the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a Special Industrial Inspection Drive in Nuh, Haryana on 03.09.2026.
Eight Flying Squads of CAQM, along with officials of the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) and the State Administration, were deployed for the special inspection drive. The teams inspected 35 industrial units/ premises across Nuh District to assess compliance with applicable environmental norms and the conditions stipulated under the Consent to Operate (CTO).
The inspection drive revealed significant instances of non-compliance. Out of the 35 units inspected, 17 units were found not complying, 11 units were found complying, and 7 units were found closed/ non-operational at the time of inspection. Out of the 11 complying units, 10 units were found fully compliant, while 1 unit was found compliant with recommendations for improvement.
During the inspections, several violations relating to air pollution abatement measures were observed. Wet scrubbers were found defective or inadequately functioning at certain units, including cases of leakage and inadequate water flow. Non-functional or poorly maintained Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) systems were also observed. In some units, inadequate stack/ chimney arrangements and insufficient stack height for boilers/ thermic fluid heaters were noticed.
The inspection teams also found several instances of inadequate measures for controlling fugitive dust. Conveyor belts were found without adequate covering, water sprinkling and dust suppression arrangements were inadequate, boundary windbreakers were insufficient and internal roads were found unpaved, resulting in generation of fugitive dust. Non-compliant DG sets were also found operating at certain units.
Further, instances of use/ burning of wood in industrial operations and use of unapproved liquid fuel in boilers/ thermic fluid heaters were observed. The inspection teams also observed cases where the required Online Continuous Emission Monitoring System (OCEMS) had not been installed, while stack emission monitoring reports were found outdated or had not been submitted.
The teams further observed instances of boilers/ thermic fluid heaters or other machinery were being operated without being covered under the applicable CTO. In addition, dense smoke/ fumes were also observed within industrial premises/ shed areas, during the inspections.
The preliminary assessment of the Special Industrial Inspection Drive indicates that the non-compliances observed in the 17 units relate to inadequate air pollution control systems, fugitive dust emissions, non-compliant DG sets, use of unapproved fuels, lack emission monitoring systems and non-adherence to CTO conditions.
The Commission has reiterated that all industrial units operating in NCR are required to strictly comply with applicable environmental norms and prescribed regulatory requirements, including maintaining effective air pollution control devices, ensuring adequate fugitive dust suppression, using only approved fuels, maintaining compliant DG sets, installing and operating requisite emission monitoring systems and adhering to applicable CTO conditions.
CAQM has further emphasized that such inspection drives are an important mechanism for assessing on-ground compliance and identifying gaps that require timely corrective action(s). The Commission will continue to undertake such intensive inspection drives across NCR to ensure that violations are identified and necessary corrective and enforcement action is taken by the concerned agencies.

The Nagpur chapter of Mining Engineers’ Association of India (MEAI) in association with Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM), a subordinate office under Ministry of Mines, Government of India would jointly organize a one-day Regional Workshop on “Approach of Transforming Data into Intelligent Governance through AI-enabled Mining Tenement System (MTS)” at Hotel Tuli International, Sadar, Nagpur on 5th September, 2026.

title: 2,306 long pending pension grievances redressed during Special Campaign 3
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: 2,306 long pending pension grievances redressed during Special Campaign 3
sources.evidenceText:
The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) is committed towards the welfare of the central government pensioners, including the meaningful and accessible redressal of their grievances. For this, annual special campaigns have been organized since 2024. In the third edition, the department started Special Campaign 3 on 7th July, 2026, for the timely and qualitative redressal of long-pending pension grievances/claims/issues. This campaign had a preparatory phase and an execution phase and concluded on 31st August, 2026.
During the preparatory phase, all ministries, departments, and their attached or subordinate offices were mandated to identify long-pending grievances, claims, and issues received via both online and physical modes. Ministries and departments identified 1,062 target cases under this phase. Further, 2,131 grievance cases pending on the CPENGRAMS portal for more than one month were also taken for redressal in this phase.
During the execution phase, the department actively coordinated with the ministries/department for redressal of these cases. Two mid-campaign review meetings were held, and the status of the pendency of these cases was sought regularly.
Coordinated efforts of 40 ministries/departments have culminated in the successful resolution of 2,306 cases out of 3,193 taken-up cases, registering the redressal rate of 72%. Active follow-up is being done for the redressal of remaining grievances.
The demographic distribution of the redressal reflects that most of the resolved cases pertain to the pensioners and family pensioners residing in rural areas. It is a healthy trend, as the redirection of grievances from rural areas in online mode through various portals operated by ministries/departments and CPENGRAMS portal, is bridging the digital divide.
The collective efforts have resulted in the successful redressal of some long-pending cases.
Some major success cases are:
1. Release of Rs. 16.70 lakh on account of family pension arrears to Ms. Jayalakshmi Karnan, the disabled dependent daughter of a Defence pensioner, with effect from June, 2013.

More than 300 waste pickers from the Najafgarh Zone participated in the programme.
The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, implemented to ensure the safety, dignity, and socio-economic upliftment of sanitation workers, including sewer and septic tank workers and waste pickers. The scheme focuses on occupational safety, formal recognition of workers, access to healthcare and social security benefits, skill development, and mechanisation of hazardous sanitation work, with the aim of eliminating hazardous manual cleaning practices across the country.

The 89th edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle will be organised in Surat on September 6, with the theme ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’, promoting fitness, sports and community participation as means to encourage a healthy and drug-free youth.

title: Geothermal Energy
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: Geothermal Energy
sources.evidenceText:
The intense heat in the Earth's interior is a powerful source of clean energy called geothermal energy. Given India's rich geothermal resources, this form of energy holds immense promise as a round-the-clock available source of power. The National Policy on Geothermal Energy aims to harness this potential. It seeks to make geothermal energy a key part of the nation's renewable energy story as India drives towards Net Zero by 2070. The recent commissioning of the first two geothermal wells in Ladakh marks the beginning of this journey.
Harnessing Geothermal Energy for a Sustainable India
Deep below the Earth's surface, emanating from the intense heat of its interiors, lies a constant, low-carbon source of energy called geothermal energy. In locations with suitable geology and tectonics, this energy can be tapped to generate power or used directly on the ground. Unlike solar and wind energy, this source provides renewable energy that is available round the clock. Recognising this potential, the Government notified the National Policy on Geothermal Energy in September 2025. The policy charts a clear roadmap for exploring and developing India's geothermal resources. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry for its implementation.
Building on this framework, India achieved a historic milestone in July 2026. The ONGC Energy Centre commissioned the country's first two geothermal wells in Puga Valley, Ladakh . At a height of over 14,000 feet above sea level, Puga Valley is among India's most promising geothermal sites, known for its hot springs and underground heat reserves. The two 1,000-metre-deep wells will support reservoir evaluation. They also pave the way for India's first 1-megawatt demonstration geothermal power project , marking the country's entry into geothermal power generation.
As India advances its clean energy transition, geothermal power offers a dependable, indigenous way to diversify the nation's renewable energy mix.
Understanding Geothermal Energy: An Overview
Geothermal Energy is a steady, low-carbon and weather-independent energy source. It holds a vast untapped resource base to strengthen India's clean energy future and cut reliance on fossil fuels.
Formation of Geothermal Energy
The Earth's interior consists of four main layers: the outermost, solid crust; the middle, semi-solid mantle; and the core divided into a dense liquid outer core and solid inner core. The temperature of the interior rises with depth - the mantle temperature reaches about 3700 Celsius degrees at its boundary with the core, while the core temperature goes up to 5000- 6000 Celsius. This heat is generated by radioactive decay of elements like uranium, thorium, and potassium, as well as residual heat left over from the planet's formation. This heat gives rise to huge convection currents in the mantle, as hot material moves up from the core boundary towards the cooler, upper parts of the mantle and crust. This material also contains water trapped as hydroxides. These convection currents give rise to all tectonic activity, including earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building. In geologically active regions, faults and fractures let the hot material travel closer to the surface. This process creates reservoirs of hot water and steam, trapped within permeable rock. This thermal energy, harnessed from within the Earth, is known as geothermal energy .
From Geothermal Energy to Power Production
Geothermal power generation converts the earth's natural heat into electricity by tapping hot water and steam trapped beneath the surface. Deep wells bring these resources up to the surface. The steam then drives a turbine connected to a generator. This process resembles conventional thermal power generation . However, it replaces fuel combustion with naturally occurring underground heat. After power generation, the used water is condensed and reinjected into the reservoir. This supports resource replenishment and enables continued energy production. Geothermal energy also supports direct heat applications across district heating, agriculture, aquaculture, and space heating & cooling, enabling efficient utilisation of geothermal heat.
Inside the Earth
From the centre outward, the Earth is structured in four distinct layers. The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel, about 2,400 km wide. The outer core surrounding it is a liquid layer of molten iron and nickel, roughly 2,400 km thick. The mantle , composed mostly of hot, dense rock, extends nearly 2,900 km and forms the largest layer. Finally, the crust is the thin, solid outer layer, ranging from about 5 to 8 kilometres thick beneath the oceans to 24 to 56 kilometres thick beneath the continents.
India's Geothermal Resource Base
India's varied geology offers a strong foundation for geothermal development. The Geological Survey of India (GSI) has mapped 381 hot springs and identified 10 geothermal provinces nationwide . India's theoretical geothermal prospect stands at nearly 10.6 GW. Of this, 42 sites have been recognised as promising for power generation and direct heat use.
The 10 geothermal provinces include the Himalayan Geothermal Province, Naga-Lusai, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Son Narmada Tapi (SONATA), West Coast, Cambay Graben, Aravalli, Mahanadi, Godavari, and South Indian Cratonic regions.
India's geothermal rift basins hold strong scope, owing to favourable geology and tectonics. But suitable projects can arise anywhere geothermal resources exist. Advanced technologies like Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) and Advanced Geothermal Systems (AGS) will further widen exploration opportunities.
Repurposing Abandoned Oil and Gas Wells
Geothermal energy can be extracted from abandoned oil and gas wells. Inactive or unproductive wells can potentially be repurposed for geothermal initiatives, subject to technical and operational feasibility. This approach builds on existing drilling expertise, well data and infrastructure from the oil and gas sector.
India’s Geothermal Expansion
India is moving from resource assessment to field demonstration with remarkable speed. This momentum is reflected in the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy sanctioning five research and development projects between July and August 2025, covering resource assessment, indigenous technology development and field demonstration. The projects span electricity generation, heating and cooling applications. These efforts are generating the technical data and field experience needed for future commercial deployment.
Project
Current Status of Government-supported Projects
as of 12 December 2026
Ankleshwar, Gujarat
A pilot project evaluating electricity generation by retrofitting unproductive oil and gas wells. Field investigations and baseline geological and production data have been completed.
Gandhinagar, Gujarat
A demonstration project integrating solar and geothermal energy has drilled three geothermal wells that produce geothermal fluid at 70 to 80°C and has demonstrated electricity generation of 50 to 90 kilowatts.
Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
Studies are underway at five geothermal sites to assess the region's geothermal resource through field investigations and geochemical analysis.
Hyderabad, Telangana
A research project is developing a geothermal cooling system for air conditioning applications using modelling and performance analysis.
Shallow Geothermal Energy
Pilot study is developing analytical models to evaluate shallow geothermal systems using Borehole Heat Exchangers for heating and cooling applications.
Significant geothermal resources, advancing technologies and early field activity are laying the foundation for a future of geothermal energy in India. While commercial-scale power generation is yet to be established, expanding well fields, demonstration activities and research and development initiatives are strengthening the ecosystem for wider deployment.
Unlocking India’s Geothermal Potential: Policy & Partnerships
Geothermal energy is a proven, established renewable technology worldwide. Global installed capacity reached 15.67 GW by the end of 2025 . Indonesia, the US, the Philippines, Türkiye and New Zealand lead the field, together holding around 67% of global capacity. India is now building a strong ecosystem to advance geothermal energy from resource assessment to real-world deployment. National programmes and international partnerships are driving this mission forward, powering research, technology development and knowledge exchange across the sector.
National Policy on Geothermal Energy, 2025
The National Policy on Geothermal Energy aims to establish geothermal energy as a major renewable pillar. It promotes systematic exploration and deployment of India's geothermal resources. The Policy prioritises research, drilling, reservoir management, and direct-use applications. It also supports Ground Source Heat Pumps (GSHPs) for heating and cooling. A clear regulatory framework encourages both public and private sector participation. The Policy facilitates repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells for geothermal use. It further supports a national geothermal data repository, pilot projects, and Centres of Excellence.
Renewable Energy Research and Technology Development Programme (RE-RTD)
MNRE is implementing the RE-RTD scheme through research institutions and industry partners. This initiative aims to develop indigenous, cost-effective technologies for renewable energy, including geothermal energy, across the country.
International Collaborations
India has advanced its geothermal energy efforts through collaborations with several international partners. Under cooperation mechanisms with Australia and Iceland , geothermal energy has been identified as a key area of cooperation. Similarly, an MoU with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia designated geothermal energy as a focus area of bilateral engagement.
These initiatives are providing a coordinated platform for translating India’s geothermal resources into scalable solutions across sectors.
New Dimension in India’s Renewable Energy Mix
India's geothermal energy journey reflects the Government's steadfast commitment to energy security and sustainable growth. From notifying the National Policy on Geothermal Energy to commissioning the country's first two geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh, India has moved decisively from planning to implementation. The country holds a theoretical geothermal resource potential of nearly 10,600 MW. Growing pilot projects and strengthening international collaborations are expanding its applications, from power generation to heating, geo-tourism and agriculture. Geothermal energy is thus emerging as a valuable addition to India's renewable energy portfolio. As India advances towards its 2070 Net Zero target, geothermal energy will remain a steady, indigenous pillar of the country's energy transition and progress.

title: NFRA Constitutes Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: NFRA Constitutes Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology
sources.evidenceText:
In keeping with Rule 15 and Rule 16 of National Financial Reporting Authority Rules 2018, which authorises National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) to form committees, study groups and task forces for effective performance of its functions under the Act, and undertake suitable measures for promotion of awareness and significance of auditing and accounting standards and audit quality, NFRA has constituted an Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology, comprising eminent experts from various fields to provide inputs and suggestions on matters that have a significant bearing on audit quality.
The Committee comprises of eminent experts, representing various stakeholder groups of NFRA- Professionals, CFOs, Audit Committees, Independent Directors, Technology Experts, Regulators and Industry.
This Advisory Committee is the third such Committee, the first being the Technical Advisory Committee, that was constituted in 2020 and whose term ended in December 2022.
In July 2024, NFRA had constituted an Advisory Group of eminent experts to advise on Auditor-Audit Committee resources, comprising the Auditor-Audit Committee Interaction (Staff) Series and outreach activities with Audit Committees and Independent Directors.
The details of the Advisory Group and Advisory Committee can be found on NFRA website at ( https://nfra.gov.in/advisory-groups-committees-of-nfra/ ).

Jai Shri Krishna!”

title: India-Belgium Joint Statement on the visit of the Prime Minister of Belgium to India
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: India-Belgium Joint Statement on the visit of the Prime Minister of Belgium to India
sources.evidenceText:
At the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Belgium, H.E. Mr. Bart De Wever, is on an official visit to India from 2-4 September 2026. The Prime Minister of Belgium is accompanied by Belgium's Minister of Defence and Foreign Trade, H.E. Mr. Theo Francken, and a high-level delegation of officials and business leaders. This is Prime Minister De Wever's first visit to India since taking office in February 2025.
Prime Minister De Wever began his visit by paying homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. Prime Minister De Wever then held bilateral talks with the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, first in a restricted format and later with their respective delegations. Their discussions ranged across the full length and breadth of the relationship between the two countries. Prime Minster Modi hosted a luncheon for Prime Minister De Wever and the visiting delegation.
The two leaders recalled the supreme sacrifice of more than 9,000 Indian soldiers in the Flanders Fields during the First World War. The two leaders also recalled that Belgium was among the first European countries to establish diplomatic relations with India in 1947. They noted that the partnership has since flourished on the foundations of shared democratic values, mutual trust, economic complementarities, and strong people-to-people ties. The leaders expressed their desire for further expanding and deepening this multifaceted relationship. The 80th anniversary of Belgium-India diplomatic relations in 2027 will give India and Belgium another historical occasion to celebrate the deepening and broadening of the bilateral relationship.
Both leaders welcomed the launch of the inaugural India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue in Brussels on 15 July 2026, co-chaired by External Affairs Minister of India and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Belgium. Anchored in the wider India-EU Strategic Partnership, they noted that the Dialogue has established a regular and comprehensive mechanism to advance cooperation across trade and investment, green transition, technology, connectivity, defence, security, and people-to-people ties. In this context, they welcomed the forthcoming Foreign Office Consultations as a key platform for advancing the priorities identified under the Strategic Dialogue.
The two leaders reiterated their call for reformed and effective multilateralism, with the United Nations Charter at its center, to sustain an equitable and peaceful international order, address pressing global challenges and prepare the world for emerging developments, including in the technological and economic domains. The two leaders stressed, in particular, the urgent need for the reform of the United Nations Security Council in order to make it more representative of today’s world. Belgium reaffirmed its support for India’s candidature for permanent membership of a reformed and expanded United Nations Security Council. Both countries agreed to support each other's candidature for non permanent membership of the UN Security Council, India for the 2028-29 term and Belgium for the 2037-2038 term.
India-EU Strategic Partnership and the Free Trade Agreement
The two Prime Ministers reaffirmed the centrality of the India-EU Strategic Partnership to India-Belgium relations. They welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations for the India-EU Free Trade Agreement during the India-EU Summit on 27 January 2026 and called for the conclusion of the negotiations on the EU-India Investment Protection Agreement and the Agreement on Geographical Indications at the earliest opportunity, with a view to further strengthening economic ties between India and the European Union.
Hailing the India-EU Free Trade Agreement as a historic milestone in the strategic partnership, the Leaders called for its timely implementation for realising the true potential for trade and investment collaboration through diversifying critical value chains and opening new markets.
The two Prime Ministers welcomed the significant progress made under the India-EU Trade and Technology Council, including its Ministerial Meeting held in Brussels in July 2026 towards forging a more integrated, resilient, and sustainable economic and technological partnership when trade and technologies are becoming increasingly intertwined. In this context, they reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening co-operation among India, Belgium, and the European Union on trade, technology, economic security, and resilient supply chains.
Both sides also endorsed the Joint India–EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda for 2030, aimed to further reinforce the strategic partnership by broadening and deepening India-EU cooperation, to deliver mutually beneficial, concrete and transformative outcomes for both partners and for the wider world. They also noted that signing of the India-EU Security and Defence Partnership will deepen strategic cooperation in areas of shared interests, including maritime security, defence industry and technology, cyber and hybrid threats, space and counter-terrorism.
Trade, Economic Cooperation and Investment
With Belgium as the 24th biggest economy in the world, and India's ambition to become a USD 10 trillion economy in the coming years, both leaders acknowledged abundant opportunities for mutually beneficial partnerships. Recognising the strong complementarities between their economies, the two Prime Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to deepening trade, investment and economic cooperation. In this context, they welcomed the steady expansion of bilateral economic ties and the growing diversification of sectors in bilateral trade, and expressed their determination to further strengthen cooperation across key sectors of shared interest, with a view to enabling the doubling of bilateral trade in the next 5 years.
The two Prime Ministers noted with satisfaction the successful Belgian Economic Mission to India in March 2025, led by Her Royal Highness Princess Astrid. They recognized the Mission as an important milestone in advancing bilateral economic engagement, fostering new partnerships between businesses and institutions, including an exchange on economic empowerment of women, and expanding cooperation in priority sectors, such as life sciences, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, energy and renewable energy, defence, aeronautics and space, logistics, transport and ports, cleantech and green engineering, chemistry, advanced materials and manufacturing, digital technologies and innovation. In this regard, they noted the strong potential of the India-Belgium partnership in the life sciences sector, building on the complementary strengths of both countries in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, clinical research, innovation and advanced healthcare solutions, and encouraged closer collaboration between industry, academia and research institutions. Both leaders agreed to keep this momentum alive through regular high-level exchanges, including with Belgium's regional trade and investment agencies.
The two leaders expressed satisfaction at the growth and diversification of bilateral economic ties and welcomed expanding cooperation in areas such as semiconductors, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, defence industrial collaboration, critical minerals refining and recycling, sustainable industries, and nuclear energy, including by exploring emerging opportunities for cooperation involving private sector stakeholders. The two leaders further acknowledged the enduring importance of the diamond trade linking Antwerp with Mumbai and Surat and agreed to further strengthen this historic partnership while pursuing new avenues for economic engagement and shared growth.
They underlined the strategic importance of maritime and port cooperation between the two countries and welcomed opportunities to deepen collaboration in port development, logistics, connectivity, dredging and offshore wind infrastructure. In this context, they welcomed the planned participation of the Flemish Minister of Mobility and Ports, Annick De Ridder, to “Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue” in New Delhi in October 2026. They also welcomed the prospect for enhanced cooperation between APEC (the Antwerp/Flanders Port Training Centre) and India's Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), particularly in areas of training needs identification and capacity building for officers and employees at all levels of management across the Indian port sector in particular and the maritime sector more broadly. They further acknowledged the continued contribution of Belgian dredging expertise to the development of India's port infrastructure and its potential role in supporting offshore renewable energy projects.
The two Prime Ministers welcomed the deepening cooperation between India and Belgium in research and higher education, including in astronomy, astrophysics and space technologies through the Belgo-Indian Network for Astronomy and Astrophysics (BINA). They also noted Belgium's contribution to several landmark astronomical facilities in India, including the Devasthal Optical Telescope, the Devasthal International Liquid Mirror Telescope, the Mount Abu Telescope and the Multi-Application Solar Telescope in Udaipur, reflecting the strength of bilateral scientific collaboration.
The two leaders welcomed the launch of the India-Belgium Investment Fast-Track Mechanism and recognized it as an important step towards further strengthening bilateral investment ties. They noted that the mechanism will serve as a dedicated platform to facilitate and expand both Belgian investments in India and Indian investments in Belgium, support businesses, address investment bottlenecks, and foster a more conducive environment for long-term economic cooperation between the two countries.
The two leaders also welcomed the ongoing engagement between the Federal Holding and Investment Company (SFPIM), Belgium’s Sovereign Wealth Fund and India’s National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF). They looked forward to formalising the collaboration between SFPIM-NIIF to help establish the Indo-Belgian economic and investment corridor. They also welcomed the contribution of the Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries (BIO Invest) and agreed to explore potential cooperation between BIO Invest and NIIF in areas of mutual interest.
The two Prime Ministers reaffirmed the importance of the India-Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Joint Economic Commission as a key mechanism for advancing bilateral economic cooperation and looked forward to its 19th Session later this year.
Defence and Security Cooperation
Prime Minister Bart De Wever conveyed Belgium's solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism, including cross-border terrorism. He once again condemned the terrorist attack on innocent civilians in Pahalgam, Jammu & Kashmir, India in April 2025. Both leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified, and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with international law. They agreed that the international community must act together, against terrorists and terrorist entities including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions regime, terrorist networks, their safe havens and their financing, including through the UN and FATF. The leaders called for strengthened international cooperation in preventing and combating terrorism, including through sanctions mechanisms at the national, regional and international levels. In this context, they expressed their intention to explore the establishment of a Belgium-India Joint Working Group on Counter-Terrorism with a view to enhancing bilateral cooperation in addressing evolving terrorist threats.
On defence cooperation, the two Prime Ministers welcomed the signing of the Letter of Intent between the two Ministries of Defence, establishing a framework for regular exchanges, staff talks, education and training, research cooperation, and defence-industrial partnerships. They noted that the agreement builds upon the understanding reached between the Defence Ministers of India and Belgium in March 2025 to institutionalize and further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation. The two leaders welcomed the steadily deepening engagement between the two defence establishments on maritime security, emerging technologies, education and military exchanges, and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. In this context, they welcomed the planned visit of Belgian Frigate LEOPOLD I to India from 5 to 8 November 2026, the intention of the Belgian Defence College to organise its World Study Trip 2027 in India and the study tour by College of Defence Management, Secunderabad to Belgium in October 2026, as concrete opportunities to further strengthen exchanges and cooperation between the two defence establishments.
They also welcomed the appointment of a Defence Attache by Belgium in New Delhi and welcomed India's decision to appoint a resident Defence Attache in the Indian Embassy in Brussels in the near future. The two leaders welcomed the steadily deepening engagement between the two defence establishments on maritime security, emerging technologies, and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.
The two Prime Ministers welcomed the growing defence-industrial cooperation between India and Belgium and noted that such partnerships were further strengthened during the Belgian Economic Mission to India in March 2025. Recognising the potential for further collaboration in defence manufacturing, technology, innovation, co-development and co-production, both leaders welcomed the signing of the multiple agreements and partnerships between the Belgian and Indian defence industries, and encouraged the industries on both sides to remain engaged.
The two leaders also noted the ongoing cooperation between the Flanders Fields Museum in Ypres and the Centre for Armed Forces Historical Research (CAFHR) in New Delhi, contributing to preserving and promoting the shared historical legacy of India and Belgium.
The two Prime Ministers welcomed the signing of the MoU between the Central Bureau of Investigation of India and the Federal Police of Belgium on cooperation in combating transnational organized crime, cybercrime, and related matters. They noted that the MoU would strengthen institutional linkages, facilitate information sharing, promote capacity building and the exchange of best practices, enhance cooperation in tracing fugitives, and deepen bilateral law enforcement cooperation in combating transnational organized crime, cybercrime, and related matters.
Green Transition, Emerging Technologies, Healthcare Cooperation and Startups
The two Prime Ministers welcomed the signing of the renewed MoU on Renewable Energy Cooperation between India and Belgium. They noted that the renewed MoU builds upon the cooperation established under the 2015 framework and the work of the Joint Working Group on Renewable Energy, and expands collaboration in key areas including green hydrogen, solar energy, energy storage, offshore wind energy, bio-energy, small hydropower and pumped storage plants.
The two countries welcomed the growing collaboration between India and Belgium in the field of green hydrogen, including industrial partnerships and knowledge exchange. They acknowledged cooperation under the Memorandum of Understanding between GH2 India, the Belgian Hydrogen Council, and Flanders Investment & Trade, as well as the active participation of Indian officials in the Egmont Institute's green hydrogen exchange programme in Brussels and reciprocal visits by government, industry, and research representatives from both countries. The leaders underscored the important role of India and Belgium in strengthening the green hydrogen value chain, including production, transportation, storage, and end-use applications, with a view to advancing decarbonisation, fostering innovation, enhancing energy security, and promoting sustainable economic growth.
Belgium and India reaffirm their commitment to the Paris Agreement its long-term goals, including the temperature goal, and its principles, including equity and common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, in the light of different national circumstances. They support a successful COP31 that advances implementation and results in enhanced action on the ground. They recognise that enhanced climate action, particularly in developing countries, is enabled by mobilising adequate, predictable and accessible climate finance from all sources, development and dissemination climate technologies and capacity-building, and underscore the importance of strengthening international cooperation in these areas. The two sides commit to strengthening climate adaptation, resilience and disaster preparedness. They further recognise the vital role of oceans and coastal ecosystems in supporting climate resilience, sustainable development and the well-being of coastal communities. Recognising the importance of strengthened ocean governance as a component of sustainable development and climate resilience, they underscored the importance of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement and broader international cooperation in maritime affairs.
The two leaders encouraged engagements between the Indian micro-electronics ecosystem, including semiconductor companies, ChipIn Centre, C-DAC, universities, and imec, Belgium. They expressed their support for these interactions to develop into deeper partnerships in semiconductor technologies, thereby contributing to the creation of resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries.
The two leaders welcomed the participation of the Minister-President of the Government of Flanders in the AI Impact Summit hosted by India, noting that the visit underscored the growing importance of cooperation in artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and innovation.
Both sides welcomed cooperation in the areas of startup incubation. In this regard, they agreed to continue collaboration between the MEITY Start Up Hub and Hub Brussels, as well as other startup hubs and skilling centers, fostering startup ecosystems, driven by supporting innovation-driven entrepreneurship, and enhancing digital skills development.
Connectivity, Mobility, Education, Culture and People-to-People Ties
Both leaders recognized the importance of underpinning people-to-people ties and connectivity with efficient visa services. In this context, they recognized the need for smooth and quick processing. As exchanges between India and Belgium are intensifying, visa processing capacity by diplomatic missions in Belgium and India will significantly increase. Given the specific need, both leaders welcomed the ongoing reinforcement of the Belgian visa delivery services in India.
Welcoming the signing of the EU MoU on Comprehensive Framework of Cooperation on Mobility and the launch of a pilot European Union Legal Gateway Office in India, the Leaders noted its role in promoting legal pathways for movement of professionals, skilled workforce and students and strengthen people-to-people ties between India and the EU. They agreed that as trade, investment, and people-to-people ties continue to grow, enhanced mobility of skilled professionals, students, researchers, and business travelers would be essential. Both leaders underscored the importance of strengthening connectivity and encouraged airline operators to explore the establishment of direct air connectivity between Belgium and India. They welcomed the ongoing cooperation between Belgian healthcare institutions and India in the healthcare sector, including initiatives facilitating the mobility of qualified nurses from India to Belgium, as well as the broader and thriving civil society cooperation between Belgium and India in the fields of healthcare and education. They encouraged continued discussions towards the signing of an MoU on Mobility and Migration.
Recalling the numerous academic partnerships formed during the Belgian Economic Mission, Prime Minister Modi invited leading Belgian Universities and premier academic institutions to open campuses in India under the New Education Policy of India. The two leaders encouraged the relevant authorities, institutions and industry stakeholders of both countries to explore cooperation between the skill development and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ecosystems of India and Belgium, including through exchange of best practices, industry-responsive training, capacity building of trainers and assessors, apprenticeships and work-based learning, cooperation in emerging and future skills, and dialogue on the alignment and recognition of qualifications, with a view to enhancing employability and supporting mutually beneficial mobility of skilled professionals. The leaders also acknowledged the contribution of the Flemish Institute for Technological Research (VITO) in promoting research cooperation, innovation, and knowledge exchange with Indian partners. They welcomed cooperation between the Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service, and the Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs of Belgium in diplomatic training.
International Issues
The two Prime Ministers also exchanged views on major international developments, including recent developments in Ukraine and in West Asia. Regarding the war in Ukraine, both sides reaffirmed their support for efforts towards the achievement of a comprehensive, just and lasting peace through dialogue and diplomacy, in accordance with the principles of the United Nations Charter and international law. On West Asia, they discussed recent developments of concern in the region and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomatic engagement to address challenges in a peaceful manner. They also stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and of maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.
The two Prime Ministers reaffirmed their shared commitment to further deepening and diversifying the India-Belgium Partnership, guided by mutual trust and a shared vision for peace, prosperity, and development. They agreed that the expanding bilateral partnership shall continue to be guided by a shared commitment to democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights, gender equality, and a rules-based international order. Building on these foundations, they expressed confidence that the India-Belgium Partnership would continue to deliver tangible benefits for both peoples and the world and also contribute to strengthening collaboration between India and Europe in addressing shared global challenges.
In the context of the deepening and diversification of the India-Belgium partnership and the increasing India-Europe engagements and India-EU ties, Prime Minister Bart De Wever extended an invitation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to undertake a bilateral visit to Belgium, at a mutually convenient time.

title: Vice-President of India Meets Seychelles Parliamentary Delegation Led by their Speaker of the National Assembly
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: Vice-President of India Meets Seychelles Parliamentary Delegation Led by their Speaker of the National Assembly
sources.evidenceText:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today met the parliamentary delegation from the Republic of Seychelles led by H.E. Ms. Azarel Ernesta, Speaker of the National Assembly of Seychelles, at Parliament House, New Delhi.
Welcoming the Speaker and the members of the delegation, the Vice President conveyed his warm greetings to the Government and the people of Seychelles on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of their country’s Independence. He also congratulated H.E. Ms. Azarel Ernesta on becoming the first woman Speaker of the Seychelles National Assembly and noted her participation in the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth (CSPOC) held in New Delhi in January 2026.
Recalling the close and enduring ties between the two countries, the Vice President said that Seychelles occupies a special place for him. He fondly remembered his visit to Seychelles for the swearing-in ceremony of President H.E. Dr. Patrick Herminie in October 2025, which was his first overseas visit as the Vice President of India. He also recalled his meetings with President Dr. Patrick Herminie and Vice President Sebastien Pillay, describing the warmth and hospitality extended by the people of Seychelles.
Highlighting the significance of 2026 in the bilateral relationship, the Vice President observed that the two countries witnessed two State Visits during the year. The Prime Minister of India participated in the 50th National Day celebrations in Seychelles in June 2026, while President Dr. Patrick Herminie paid a State Visit to India in February 2026. He further noted that Vice President Sebastien Pillay visited India in February 2026 to attend the AI Impact Summit. The Vice President also underlined that both countries are celebrating 50 years of diplomatic relations this year and expressed confidence that the current visit by the Seychelles parliamentary delegation would impart further momentum to the growing bilateral partnership.
The Vice President also recalled that in February 2026, India announced a Special Economic Package of USD 175 million for Seychelles which would elevate the development and security partnership between the two countries to new heights.
The Vice President also shared the initiatives being undertaken by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat towards modernisation and digitisation. He referred to the increasing digitisation of parliamentary functioning, simultaneous translation of proceedings into multiple languages, efforts to make parliamentary proceedings paperless and more efficient, regular capacity building programmes in cyber security, and the creation of digital archives of parliamentary texts. He conveyed India’s willingness to share its experience and knowledge with the Seychelles National Assembly and offered to organise study visits and customised capacity building programmes in accordance with the needs and priorities of Seychelles.
Emphasizing the importance of people-to-people relations, the Vice President acknowledged the contribution of the Indian diaspora in Seychelles, particularly the Gujarati and Tamil communities, noting that they serve as an enduring bridge of friendship between the two nations.
The Vice President noted that the Speaker of the Seychelles National Assembly regularly practises Yoga and remarked that Yoga serves as a strong symbol of the close people-to-people relationship between India and Seychelles and looked forward to continued engagement and closer cooperation between the two parliamentary institutions in the years ahead. He wished the Speaker and the members of the delegation a pleasant and productive stay in India.

title: National Institute of Homoeopathy, Kolkata Celebrates Golden Jubilee
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: National Institute of Homoeopathy, Kolkata Celebrates Golden Jubilee
sources.evidenceText:
The National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH), Kolkata today celebrated its Golden Jubilee, marking 50 years of dedicated service in homoeopathic education, research and patient care. As part of the celebrations, a state-of-the-art Modular Operation Theatre and a Centre of Excellence were inaugurated, significantly strengthening the Institute’s clinical, academic and research infrastructure.
The celebrations were graced by Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and Shri Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education. Jyotirmay Singh Mahato and Samik Bhattacharya, Members of Parliament, and Sumana Sarkar, MLA, Government of West Bengal, along with Sh. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha , Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, senior officials, faculty members, doctors, students and other stakeholders, were also present on this occasion.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that completion of 50 years is a significant milestone in the journey of NIH Kolkata. He said the Golden Jubilee is not only an occasion to acknowledge the Institute’s achievements but also an opportunity to chart its priorities for the coming decades.
The Minister said that the newly inaugurated facilities reflect the Government’s commitment to strengthening Ayush institutions with modern infrastructure, quality education, advanced research capabilities and improved patient-care facilities. He emphasised the need to integrate the strengths of traditional systems of medicine with contemporary technology, research and innovation to address emerging healthcare requirements.
Shri Jadhav also underlined the importance of strengthening homoeopathic education and research and creating greater opportunities for students, researchers and young professionals. He expressed confidence that NIH Kolkata would further consolidate its position as a leading institution in homoeopathic education, research and patient care.
Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education, highlighted NIH Kolkata’s five-decade contribution to education and healthcare. He said the new facilities would further strengthen the Institute as an academic and professional centre and provide enhanced opportunities for learning, training and innovation.
Jyotirmay Singh Mahato, said the expansion of NIH would contribute to improved clinical services and healthcare access for people in Kolkata and surrounding areas.
Rajya Sabha MP Samik Bhattacharya, said the new facilities would enable the Institute to build on its strong institutional foundation and respond effectively to future academic and healthcare requirements.
The newly inaugurated Modular Operation Theatre adds a significant dimension to the Institute’s clinical infrastructure. Designed in accordance with contemporary healthcare requirements and equipped with modern systems, the facility will strengthen NIH Kolkata’s capacity to provide advanced clinical services while supporting training and professional development.
The Centre of Excellence will further enhance the Institute’s capabilities in clinical research, academic development and innovation. It will provide a platform for advancing research, fostering institutional collaborations and creating enhanced opportunities for students, faculty and healthcare professionals.
Dr. Pralay Sharma, Director, NIH Kolkata, said that the new facilities demonstrate NIH’s commitment to strengthening its infrastructure and preparing for the next phase of growth in homoeopathic education, research and patient care.
Ayush Minister Interacts with Students
During his visit to NIH on September 2, 2026, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, also held an extensive interaction with students of the institute to understand their views, concerns and suggestions for further development of homoeopathy.
During the interaction, students highlighted the academic environment and extensive clinical exposure available at NIH, including opportunities to learn from a large and diverse patient base. The Minister also acknowledged the contribution of postgraduate trainees and interns to patient-care activities. The Minister took note of suggestions relating to strengthening institutional infrastructure, including the proposed hospital building, animal house and pharmaceutical analysis laboratory. Issues concerning stipends, housestaffship and the NTET examination were also discussed.

title: “ELCs will empower the Youth to uphold Truth and Strengthen Democracy”: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
indiaConnection: This release is an official Government of India public record.

sources.title: “ELCs will empower the Youth to uphold Truth and Strengthen Democracy”: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
sources.evidenceText:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised its fourth regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINet" in Goa today, focusing on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens. Addressing the gathering, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar said that the students are the future of India. He added that Electoral Literacy Clubs across India will help strengthen the world's largest democracy.
Addressing the students and teachers from schools, colleges and universities across Goa, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated that ELCs are important platforms for students to understand electoral processes and democratic values.
The Chief Election Commissioner also underlined that elections in India are held strictly as per the Constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and are conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of recognised political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages.
CEC also highlighted ECINet as the vehicle of transparency for electors across the country, providing a unified digital platform for election-related services and information.
ELC 2.0, with the tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.", reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities, encouraging young and first-time voters to understand and meaningfully participate in democracy. Leveraging the extensive ECINet digital platform, which provides all election-related services from roll to poll, the initiative will drive continuous, year-round electoral literacy activities through a dedicated ELC portal, building a streamlined pan-India network of ELCs.
The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.
Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also disseminate information on electoral registration, polling, counting, ECINet App and other key ECI initiatives.
CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar was on a two-day visit to Goa to interact with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and ELC members from across the State. Yesterday, during an interactive session with over 1,000 BLOs, he commended their dedicated service and contribution to the smooth conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls in the State.
The students also had a Question-and-Answer session with the CEC as part of the meeting.
